newsitem.title: FINLAND: Forestry prospects still unclear - UPM, Metsaliitto.
newsitem.headline: Forestry prospects still unclear - UPM, Metsaliitto.

text.p: Finnish forestry groups UPM-Kymmene and Metsaliitto said on Tuesday the forest industry's cyclical outlook is still uncertain despite recent pulp price increase anouncements.

"The outlook is largely as uncertain (as in October), nothing special has occurred since then," UPM-Kymmene CEO Juha Niemela told Reuters, asked if there had been any change since the company voiced uncertainty about pulp price prospects in October.

Forestry groups Enso Oy and Metsaliitto said earlier on Tuesday they were likely to follow Sweden's Sodra and Norway's Norske Skog by raising prices of softwood market pulp to $610 per tonne from $560 at the beginning of 1997.
Niemela declined to estimate whether the planned price increases could hold.
"Announcements on price increases are traditionally made amid uncertainty on whether they can materialise. We just have to hope that the timing is correct this time," he said.

Antti Oksanen, CEO of Metsa-Serla Oy's parent company Metsaliitto agreed the industry's prospects have remained uncertain, but said the recent pulp price hikes had decreased fears about a renewed fall in the prices.
"At least this means that an expected double dip ... is not expected to take place," Oksanen said.
Oksanen said some improvement had also been seen in the sawn goods industry's prospects.
"But how enduring this is will depend largely on how gross domestic products in Europe develop," he said.
